Inspect native axial amplitude slices

Scrub consecutive source depth bins from about 1.0 to 1.7 m. These are slices through the reconstructed volume, not filled surfaces. Click a pixel or focus the image and use arrow keys to inspect its source-array location.

Amplitude display uses 8 bits and the global volume maximum. Full precision: volume.npy. Gray 0 can mean amplitude rounded to zero. It is not a free-space determination.

Selected pixel: axial profile and threshold sensitivity

The curve uses the same consecutive, 8-bit display frames as the slice viewer, only inside the plotted depth window. Markers and the table use the full-precision full volume, before quantization. A rounded curve can appear to cross a threshold at a different bin.

Black: display amplitude /255 · Purple: default 4.5 threshold and its exact native first crossing · Gray: other native crossings · Amber: current slice

Interpretation limits

  • Published released-code route port, not a new f-k or adaptive-sampling method.
  • Paper Methods describes a ±30 kHz band-pass absent from released Fig2 scripts; input prefilter status is unknown.
  • No native MATLAB numerical-output equivalence established; small independent arithmetic checks and qualitative published comparison only.
  • Source coordinates/depth are unregistered: no relay-wall/world transform, time-zero offset or independently calibrated sound speed.
  • Published figure depth labels differ; no guessed calibration offset applied.
